admission.authority: direct user continuation of the main-backed BRC multiplier transport program plus exact odd-N mod-8 scan reduction
admission.reason: Strict extension of exact multiplier root/remainder transport: odd-N mod-4 impossibility, exact m=4 mod 8 witness reduction to m/4, structural same-parity factor-pair priority, and direct m=1 to target-m BRC jumps.

methods.name: BRC prioritized direct multiplier jump / mod-8 irredundant scan
capabilities: exact elimination of odd-N multipliers m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 as impossible difference-of-squares targets
exact reduction of every successful immediate witness at m congruent 4 mod 8 to the smaller multiplier m/4 with the same gcd factor
scan-complete odd-N multiplier representative residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8
same-parity multiplier factor-pair structural scoring on the exact representative set
direct exact BRC transport from the retained m=1 root/remainder state to arbitrary target m<=100
proved at-most-11 odd-basin corrections for direct jumps
candidate ordering that does not require materializing all intermediate multiplier states
methods.core_law: For odd N, m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 is impossible as a difference of squares. If m=4*l with l odd and the immediate ceiling-square test succeeds, x and y are even; dividing by two gives an immediate ceiling witness at l=m/4 and preserves the gcd factor because N is odd. Hence residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8 form a scan-complete representative set. For any target t<=100, the dyadic predictor floor(2^B(sqrt(t)-1)) applied to the retained m=1 BRC root places floor(sqrt(tN)) at most 11 odd square-basin crossings above the candidate; the exact remainder update uses R+(t-1)N-d(2J+d).
methods.hard_boundary: Difference-of-squares feasibility and scan irredundancy are distinct: m congruent 4 mod 8 is feasible but redundant, while m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 is impossible. The mod-8 reduction and direct jump are exact; the same-parity factor-pair ranking is only a finite empirically useful heuristic and is not claimed optimal. Multiplier-Fermat/Hart/Lehman remains classical prior art. No global novelty priority, asymptotic factorization speedup, theorem about semiprime ratio distributions, or Foundation promotion is claimed.
